title: Every Polish group has a non-trivial topological group automorphism
summary: Comprehensive verification using text, math, citation, and cross-section consistency verifiers found no critical errors in this paper. The mathematical proofs are logically sound: Proposition 2.1 correctly handles non-Boolean groups via conjugation and inversion; Lemma 2.2 provides a valid extension result for automorphisms on dense subgroups of Polish groups; Lemma 2.3's proof correctly applies Zorn's lemma to construct the required identity neighborhood; and the proof of Theorem 1.1 validly builds a non-trivial automorphism on a dense subgroup and extends it to the whole group. All key citations were verified via web search: Barit & Renaud (1978), van Mill (1983), Effros (1965), Ungar (1975), and Rosendal (2005) all exist and are correctly attributed. The paper is internally consistent across all sections — the abstract matches the main results, lemmas are used correctly in subsequent proofs, and there are no contradictions between any sections. The paper generalizes the Barit-Renaud result from locally compact groups to all Polish groups using elementary methods, answering Forte Shinko's question.
